name: 41429-badwordsdecode-0.6b-1gpu
hardware: 1x H100 80GB HBM3 (one GPU of an a3 node, `--gres=gpu:1`), sm90. Run on an otherwise idle node; see the seal in env.yaml.
parallelism: TP=1, PP=1, DP=1, `--distributed-executor-backend uni`, one GPU.
load_profile: concurrent (closed loop), streams=64, rate unbounded, warmup the first 10%, bounded at 640 requests with a 2700 s safety cap.
workload: guidellm `synthetic_text`, SINGLE TURN, no shared prefix: exactly 256 prompt tokens and exactly 256 output tokens, min = max on both, seed 1, `request_format: plain` so no chat template is applied. Every request carries `bad_words` = 100 distinct strings, each of which is exactly one Qwen3 token, at temperature 1.0 and top_p 1.0. `SamplingParams.update_from_tokenizer` expands each string into a bare and a space-prefixed variant and keeps both when they tokenize to different single ids, so the engine enforces 200 distinct banned ids per request, not 100.
purpose: A small-model content-safe text generator producing fixed 256-token replies with 100 banned words, 64 concurrent streams, one GPU.
launch:
# The engine's command line. One small dense model on one GPU, one process.
model: Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B
tensor-parallel-size: 1
distributed-executor-backend: uni

# Pinned rather than left to the defaults: the engine runs in-process (guidellm's `vllm_python`
# backend) under a usage context that the `vllm serve` batch-default table does not cover, so an
# unpinned engine resolves to a different operating point. Neither can bind at this load.
max-num-batched-tokens: 8192
max-num-seqs: 1024

# Prompts are drawn independently, so there is no prefix to reuse.
enable-prefix-caching: false

# A request is 256 prompt + 256 output tokens; the checkpoint declares 40960.
max-model-len: 2048

# This engine's own default, written down so a change of default cannot move the KV pool.
gpu-memory-utilization: 0.90
